Hello everyone! It’s time for the action of Day 2 between Sri Lanka and New Zealand. The highlight of Day 1 was predicted tthat the rain will hamper the proceedings but turned out the new rising star of Lanka, Kamindu Mendis yet again showed his immense maturity to notch a brilliant ton against the Kiwis. He looked well oiled for a big score but fell right at the end of Day 1 which has given the Kiwis a bit of hope to run through the tail quickly and restrict Lanka under 350.
...DAY 2, SESSION 1...

Right then, the first day of this Test match has remained unscathed even after chances of rain throughout the day and we have had 88 overs worth of play. The average first-innings total at Galle is about 365 runs and Sri Lanka seem to be heading close to that but with the loss of Kamindu Mendis, they will have to be watchful on Day 2. Can the Kiwis regroup and knock over the Lankan tail early on Day 2? Only time will tell. Join us on Thursday at 3.30 am GMT for the build-up of Day 2 with the cricketing action scheduled to begin at 4.30 am GMT.

New Zealand were very competitive with the ball in the first two sessions but everyone knew that the pitch would flatten out, especially after Tea and that's what happened but their frontline spinners didn't do much justice either. Ajaz Patel had a torrid time after his initial spell of 10 overs and whilst Mitchell Santner bowled tight, he didn't look like picking up a wicket. Young pacer, William O'Rourke was the star with 3 wickets and towards the end, Patel did come back to get the crucial wicket of Kamindu Mendis as all-rounder Glenn Phillips did a lot of the heavy lifting to make up the overs and bowled decently well too.

The final session was Lanka's best in terms of not just runs scored but the scoring rate as well which ensured, they knocked over 300 plus runs on Day 1 and set up the Test match nicely. Kamindu Mendis was the star of the show with a score of 50 or more now in all of his 7 Tests and his partnership worth 103 runs along with Kusal Mendis was the backbone of Lanka's first innings. Kusal fell after reaching his fifty but Kamindu went on to score a stellar ton before falling to a fine delivery a few minutes before the end of the day's play which has now allowed New Zealand to just sneak back into the game.

What a day of Test cricket we have witnessed in Galle. It was engrossing and things ebbed and flowed at a brisk pace and at the end of it all, hosts Sri Lanka will be the happier of the two sides heading into Day 2 not by much though.

Commentary.Commentary: We’re back for the final session of what has been a thrilling opening day of this Test match. The umpires out and in position, while the Kiwis take to the field, eager to capitalize on their momentum and finish the day strong. Kamindu Mendis is now joined by Kusal Mendis at the crease, and this duo carries the crucial responsibility of steering their side out some trouble. William O'Rourke will complete his over.
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

More of the same is what the Kiwis will be looking for. The wicket is providing a lot of assistance and they’ll just need to continue to hit the right areas and be patient. Sri Lanka on the other hand, will hope someone can hang around with Mendis and take them to that 300-run mark which will be a good first-innings score on this wicket. Join us for what could be a vital third session in a bit. However, dark clouds now loom large over Galle and hopefully, the rain stays away.

New Zealand will be very pleased with their work in this session! Had it not been for the wicket of Angelo Mathews right towards the end, we would have called it a shared session but now, we have to give it to the Kiwis. They began brilliantly as they got Dinesh Chandimal and Dhananjaya de Silva early after the Lunch break. Then there was a solid partnership between Kamindu Mendis and Angelo Mathews which seemed like taking the hosts to safer shores. Just at the stroke of Lunch though, William O'Rourke struck, he got rid of Mathews to ensure his team entered the break as the happier side.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! What a time to strike and William O'Rourke is the man yet again who does the job for his side. O'Rourke hits the deck hard again at a brisk pace and the ball seems to be nipping away. Angelo Mathews presses back and goes fishing at a relatively wide one but the ball holds its line and the outside edge is found. The ball nestles into the gloves of Tom Blundell behind the stumps and Mathews has to walk back for a hard-fought 36(116). That will be Tea on Day 1 as well.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the post-Lunch session on Day 2! The update on Angelo Mathews is that he is in pain but it isn't bad and he hasn't gone for any X-rays which means we might see him again in the first innings. The umpires and the players are back on the field. Dinesh Chandimal and Kamindu Mendis are set to resume their stay at the crease for Sri Lanka. And, it will be Tim Southee to begin proceedings with the ball after the break.
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

Right then, 88 runs in that first session and a couple of wickets fell too but expect the upcoming session to aid the batters as the pitch will be basking in the sun and will flatten out more. The spinners will be key and we might see a good battle between bat and ball just like in the first session. Do join us as 7.10 am GMT for the post-Lunch session.

At the Lunch break, New Zealand will feel they could have done a bit better given how things started for them. It was always going to a track that was good for batting but the extra grass left on the surface meant that the pacers had something to smile about early on. Young pacer William O'Rourke made good use of the extra pace and bounce and picked up a couple of wickets in the first 10 overs before the spinners came in. Ajaz Patel remained economical but wasn't quite able to create wicket-taking opportunities. The Kiwis will now look to regroup and hope the others come into the mix as O'Rourke has already bowled 9 overs.

Sri Lanka opted to bat first as is the general norm in Galle and were quick to get out of the blocks thanks to some positive intent shown by Pathum Nissanka. However, Dimuth Karunaratne looked shaky and was the first to fall before Nissanka too joined him after a few overs. Dinesh Chandimal and Angelo Mathews then led the fightback and seemed very comfortable out there in the middle, with the odd delivery bothering them. Mathews had to retire hurt after a stinging blow to the right index finger and since his departure, Kamindu Mendis has come in and played a few authoritative strokes, allowing Chandimal to play within himself.

End of an engrossing first session of this Test match and at the end of it, both teams will be decently pleased with their efforts. The scoring rate has been decent and the over rate has been pretty good as despite the threat of rain before the game, things have moved along quickly.

Commentary.Commentary: Half a shout for LBW but seemed to be going down leg. Southee floats it up on the pads, looking for that magical away swinger but the ball slides on and clips the back pad of Pathum Nissanka before rolling away past short fine leg. They get a leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Tim Southee to Pathum Nissanka, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Similar length, just a tad outside off, Pathum Nissanka presses back and gently blocks it away towards covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Tim Southee to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Oh, inside edge right away! Southee bowls this one just short of a good length and on off, gets the ball to nip away and gets additional bounce as well. Pathum Nissanka looks to defend off the back foot but gets an inside edge that goes past the stumps and into the fine leg fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Tim Southee to Pathum Nissanka, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the game to begin! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of New Zealand who form a huddle before taking their places on the field. It will be the pair of Dimuth Karunaratne and Pathum Nissanka to open the innings for Sri Lanka. Skipper, Tim Southee well take the new ball for the Kiwis and is raring to go. Three slips and a gully in place, let's go...

We are just a few minutes away from the start of this Test match but first, the two sets of players will line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of New Zealand first, followed by that of Sri Lanka.

PITCH REPORT - Farvez Maharoof is pitchside. He says that the conditions look fantastic and goes on to say that the pitch looks the same and adds that there is a lot of grass on the pitch which will aid the pacers early on. Mentions that a big first innings score is always crucial in Galle.

Tim Southee, the captain of New Zealand says that when you come to this part of the world you want to bat first and adds that they have a couple of proper spinners and a couple of batters who can bowl spin and it's nice to get back to Test cricket.

Dhananjaya de Silva, the captain of Sri Lanka says that they will bat first the fourth innings will be difficult and adds that they are going in with 2 proper spinners and 2 fast bowlers. Adds that the team is motivated and is looking forward to this competition.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tom Latham, Devon Conway, Kane Williamson, Rachin Ravindra, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Blundell (WK), Glenn Phillips, Mitchell Santner, Tim Southee (C), Ajaz Patel, William O'Rourke.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Dimuth Karunaratne, Pathum Nissanka, Dinesh Chandimal, Angelo Mathews, Kamindu Mendis, Dhananjaya de Silva (C), Kusal Mendis (WK), Ramesh Mendis, Prabath Jayasuriya, Lahiru Kumara, Asitha Fernando.
TOSS - Sri Lanka win the toss and will BAT first.

Right then, as many as 24 WTC points are up for grabs and both sides will be looking to make the most of this series. Also, with the threat of rain looming large, the toss could prove to be crucial and with both teams expected to field three frontline spinners, we can expect the pitch to turn from Day 1 itself. Stay tuned as the toss and team sheets are coming up soon, weather permitting that is.

Sri Lanka on the other hand will be in a much more positive mood with that uplifting Test match win against England away from home at the Oval and even though they lost that series, they will be looking to build a fortress at home as they took have an outside chance of making it to the WTC final. They have a good record at home in the recent past and with spin-friendly conditions on offer, the Lankans will be feeling good about their chances and have gone ahead and announced their playing XI as well.

New Zealand have had a torrid time since their arrival in the subcontinent with their One-off Test against Afghanistan getting washed off without a single ball being bowled and they now have to somehow win at least one game at Galle, where they have never won to keep their WTC hopes alive. However, the bigger concern seems to be the weather which has followed the Kiwis from Greater Noida.
